issues.claim: Round 4 wrote both regrowth branches of a raised way's repair beside a crossing station. V06 §3.19.2 (5) (V06 l. 2935–2943, the END of VEW-r3-04): 'beside a crossing station whose stretch is `breached` or `dismantled`, a `repairWall` of that stretch first, in the same batch, … a `dismantled` stretch taking the op's bend, a new stretch drawn on its line (V06 §2.8) — so no deck stands on a fallen wall'. The `dismantled` stretch is reachable on the ordinary decline and regrowth path. T114-3's new clause (base l. 18469–18471) lets a crossing station whose spans have both fallen keep its stretch 'as a wall run', and T-V6-11's second run (V06 l. 4119) dismantles it by `absorbWall` 'from the epoch after both spans beside its crossing station have fallen'. A raised way whose reason is live again is then repaired by (5). Only the `breached` branch has a bar: T114-3's landfall clause on T-V5-14 (V05 l. 2556–2562), by hand and by V06 §3.19.2 (5). The `dismantled` branch runs a different op, `repairWall`'s bend drawing a new stretch on the line, and no bar or volume test runs it. T-V6-11 runs a hand `repairRaised` on a dismantled span and a hand `repairWall` on a dismantled stretch, each alone; T-V6-61 runs ruined spans with no station; T-V6-73 runs only the station's decay. The model seat's round-4 HAND-OFF to scope names this fixture ('a `repairRaised` beside a station whose stretch is `dismantled` (the stretch re-laid with the deck, never a deck on a gap)'). Its sibling fixture (a locked Re-derive) is the peer's VM-R4T-02; this one is open. Principle (11): an untested edge is a MAJOR.

The runs sentence (l. 18491): 'Volume 6 runs T114-1 – T114-5 save T114-3's landfall clause, …' keeps T114-3's regrowth clause with volume 6 (T-V6-73). §13.8's T114-1 – T114-5 row adds 'and T114-3's regrowth clause on volume 6's engine' to its tier cell.
